The problem, in your words

How it runs

Three stages, one chain.

Stage 01

Demand generation

Targeted Meta and TikTok campaigns optimised for WhatsApp conversations, built on verified buyer and tenant data — income, location, behaviour. Creative refreshed every 14–21 days so performance doesn’t decay quietly.

Stage 02

Lead qualification

Automated WhatsApp workflows asking budget, timeline, unit type and intent. Every lead is auto-tagged Hot, Warm or Not Ready before a salesperson spends a minute on it.

Sales handover

Pre-qualified, segmented leads routed to your agents with full context. Site visits booked directly to calendar. A live pipeline dashboard tracks the full journey, from first contact to closed unit.

Scope the engagement

The build

What the engagement actually covers.

01

Live campaign performance analysis

Working directly in your Meta and TikTok Ads Manager: locating CPL, reach and conversation volume, then connecting that live data to lead volume, lead quality and downstream conversions. The team learns to read their own numbers unaided.

02

Channel-to-offer matching

Establishing from data which platform suits which product, programme or segment — and why. Different channels reliably attract different buyer profiles; the team learns to see that pattern and allocate budget accordingly instead of guessing.

03

Lead qualification automation build

Building the WhatsApp automation workflows that qualify inbound leads before a salesperson spends a minute. A separate flow per product line, routing logic from entry trigger through to sales notification. The team builds these in the session, not afterwards.

04

Spotting the commercial opportunity in the pipeline

Teaching the team to recognise when an inbound enquiry is a corporate or B2B opportunity rather than an individual customer, and to route it to the right pipeline. Paid channels routinely surface higher-value opportunities than the campaign was built for; most organisations miss them entirely.

05

Capacity and sustainability calibration

Diagnosing whether lead volume matches what the team can actually work, and calibrating daily budgets to a sustainable pace. Turning campaigns off to cope with volume kills the pipeline that fills future intakes — the fix is calibration plus automation.

06

Attribution reporting — built by each participant

Every team member builds their own report running spend → leads → CPL → conversions → revenue, plus a cross-platform view putting Meta and TikTok side by side: which platform, which offer, which budget.

07

Full SOP handover

Written, walkthrough-tested SOPs for Meta campaign setup, creative refresh and performance review; the same framework applied to TikTok; managing and troubleshooting the automation flows; and the lead handoff process from qualified-lead notification through first call to CRM update.

08

Capstone

Each participant presents their own campaign data in impact-report format. The engagement ends with the team demonstrating the capability — not being told they have it.

Questions I get asked

Not in the lecture sense. I build the commercial engine with the team — campaigns, qualification automation, sales handover, reporting — while training them to run every part of it. They leave having built it, not having watched it.

Built around a core team; four or more participants is the usual scoping. Fewer than four is usually better served by the Growth Strategy Day, which you can also bring your two or three people to for KES 10,000 each.

Yes. Every participant builds their own attribution report and presents their campaign data in impact-report format as the capstone.

Our campaigns generate more leads than the team can handle. Is that a fit?

That’s one of the clearest signals of fit. The instinct is to switch campaigns off, which kills the pipeline that fills future intakes. The answer is calibrating budget to a sustainable pace and putting automation in front of the sales team so they only work qualified leads.

What automation do you build?

WhatsApp lead qualification workflows, with a separate flow per product or programme line. They qualify inbound leads on budget, timeline and intent before a salesperson spends time on them, then route the qualified ones to the right person with full context.

Can it be run remotely?

It’s designed as in-person working sessions. Ask and I’ll advise on what’s possible for your situation.

Do you work outside Nairobi?

Acquire & Close travels. Tell me where you are.

Tell me what your team sells.

What you sell, who does the selling, how many would be in the room, and whether anyone can currently tell you what a lead costs. That’s enough for me to scope it.

The day

Three blocks. Three distinct bodies of work.

Block 01

Paid Ads

  • Campaign structure — setting the ad account up correctly
  • Targeting — finding and speaking to the ideal customer
  • Budgeting — allocating spend so it works, not just moves
  • Creative strategy — what actually makes people stop and act
  • Reading the data — knowing what’s working before a shilling is wasted
  • A live walkthrough setting up a real campaign
Block 02

Digital Strategy

  • Mapping what your funnel should actually look like, end to end
  • Sequencing content and ads so they build on each other instead of competing for attention
  • Where each channel’s job starts and stops
Block 03

Revenue Strategy

  • Pipeline management — what happens to a lead from first interest to payment
  • Reverse-engineering the revenue goal into the specific daily actions your team can take to close the gap
  • A working plan you can hand your team on Monday morning

Why a whole day?

Those are three distinct bodies of work and each needs its own depth, not a rushed pass. A full day gives the pacing to build the plan block by block, and the follow-through to make it usable the moment you walk out.

Who it’s for

SME owners, founders and operators running ads, posting content and chasing leads without any of it connecting to a revenue number. Come on your own, or bring the people who will actually execute the plan — the marketer, the salesperson, the operations lead — for KES 10,000 each. You don’t need to already be running ads; the day suits people already spending and people about to start.

Home / About

I’m in ad accounts every day. That’s why the systems survive contact with the market.

I’m Vanessa Wanjiku — founder of Videogram Kenya. For the past seven years I’ve built high-performing campaigns for growth-focused businesses across Kenya, and behind the scenes I’ve contributed to engineering the marketing strategies of some of the country’s biggest brands.

I’m not a consultant who hands you a deck and disappears. I’m in ad accounts every day, running live campaigns for real businesses on real budgets — which is why the systems I build survive contact with the market.

Every company I sit down with can tell me, to the shilling, what they spent last quarter. Almost none can tell me what it brought back. I rebuild that chain end to end — demand, qualification, handover, measurement — then train the team to run it and document it so it survives whoever leaves.

What I refuse to do

I don’t take on work without an advertising budget. Organic growth is slow and unpredictable, and you cannot hit a revenue target on unpredictable. A demand generation engine has to be predictable and scalable, and that requires spend, deliberately deployed. If you have no ad budget and no intention of building one, say so — I’ll point you to the Growth Strategy Day rather than sell you something that won’t work.

What makes this different from an agency

Agencies build dependency. I build capability and transfer it. Every engagement ends with your team owning the system, the documentation and the dashboard. The promise isn’t “stay with me forever” — it’s “I’ll make myself unnecessary.”
